source_text: Ἡ ἐκκλησία τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ παροικοῦσα Ῥώμην τῆ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ τῇ παροικούσῃ Κόρινθον, κλητοῖς ἡγιασμένοις ἐν θελήματι θεοῦ διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ παντοκράτορος θεοῦ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ πληθυνθείη.
thought_title: Greeting from the Roman church to the Corinthian church
orientation: The letter opens with the Roman church's formal greeting to the Corinthian church, invoking grace and peace from God through Jesus Christ.
pass_a_gloss: The church of God, the [one] sojourning [in] Rome, to the church of God, the [one] sojourning [in] Corinth, to [the] called [ones], [who have been] sanctified in [the] will of God through our Lord Jesus Christ. Grace to you and peace from [the] almighty God through Jesus Christ may [it] be multiplied.

lemmas.gloss: sojourning, dwelling as a resident alien

choices.why: The participle conveys the church's status as resident aliens on earth, a key early Christian self-understanding; 'sojourning' preserves the temporary-dwelling sense.
Standard English rendering of the divine title; 'all-ruling' is more literal but less idiomatic in a greeting formula.
The optative expresses a wish; the passive voice is preserved, and 'multiplied' keeps the quantitative sense of the verb.

pass_b_english: The church of God that sojourns in Rome writes to the church of God that sojourns in Corinth, to those who are called and sanctified in the will of God through our Lord Jesus Christ. May grace and peace from almighty God be multiplied to you through Jesus Christ.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening as a formal letter greeting by making the sender and recipients explicit, and smoothed the sentence flow for modern readers.
Clarified that the church in Rome is the sender and the church in Corinth is the recipient, and smoothed the sentence flow for reading aloud.
